entry.summary: Researchers have created AI-generated videos aimed at optimally activating targeted brain regions. This approach leverages artificial intelligence to tailor visual stimuli that can influence neural activity in precise areas of the brain. The project explores the intersection of AI and neuroscience to better understand and potentially manipulate brain function through customized video content.

entry.title: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 family with flagship Sol model offering improved intelligence, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness across coding, knowledge work, and science [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI has released the GPT-5.6 family of models, including the flagship Sol, Terra, and Luna variants, designed to deliver more intelligence per token and stronger performance at lower costs. GPT-5.6 Sol achieves state-of-the-art results in coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity, and scientific tasks, outperforming previous models and competitors while reducing token usage and estimated costs. The new models also introduce an ultra setting that coordinates multiple agents to accelerate complex workflows. The GPT-5.6 models underwent extensive evaluation and safety testing before general availability, combining human red teaming and automated checks to enhance safeguards against misuse without limiting legitimate applications. GPT-5.6 Sol sets new benchmarks on professional workflow evaluations and coding agent indexes, offering faster task completion and improved cost efficiency. The family includes smaller models, Terra and Luna, which provide affordable intelligence options with competitive performance. OpenAI also introduced Programmatic Tool Calling in the Responses API to enable more efficient tool-heavy tasks by filtering intermediate data and adapting workflows dynamically.

entry.title: SK Hynix raises $26.5 billion in largest US foreign IPO, faces calls to build new semiconductor fabs in the US [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: SK Hynix completed a $26.5 billion initial public offering on the Nasdaq, marking the largest US debut by a non-American company. The IPO attracted strong demand, with shares opening 14% above the offering price, reflecting investor interest in the company's role as a key supplier of memory chips for AI processors. The funds raised will support new manufacturing facilities and advanced equipment in South Korea, while US officials have urged SK Hynix and Samsung to invest in building semiconductor fabrication plants in the United States to strengthen domestic chip production amid growing AI chip demand. This follows commitments by US memory maker Micron to invest $250 billion in new US manufacturing and create over 90,000 jobs.

entry.title: Tencent in talks to acquire majority stake in AI startup Manus at $2 billion valuation after Beijing blocked Meta's acquisition [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Tencent is negotiating to buy a majority stake in AI agent startup Manus at the same $2 billion valuation after Chinese regulators forced Meta to unwind its acquisition of the company. Manus, which operates independently out of Singapore and reported nearly $500 million in annual revenue, is seen by Tencent as complementary to its AI agent plans, including integration with WeChat. China blocked Meta's Manus acquisition in April, citing violations of investment rules and banning foreign investment in the company, describing the deal as a threat to China's technology base. The move reflects broader tensions in the AI sector between China and the U.S., with officials framing AI advancements as critical to national security.

entry.title: Google launches LiteRT.js for high-performance AI inference in web browsers using WebAssembly and hardware acceleration [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google has introduced LiteRT.js, a JavaScript binding of its LiteRT runtime that enables high-performance AI model inference directly in web browsers. This new tool allows developers to run TensorFlow Lite (.tflite) models locally with enhanced privacy, zero server costs, and low latency by leveraging hardware acceleration across CPU, GPU, and NPU via WebAssembly and APIs like WebGPU and WebNN. LiteRT.js supports easy integration with JavaScript and TypeScript applications and offers improved performance over previous solutions like TensorFlow.js by using native runtime optimizations such as XNNPACK for CPUs and ML Drift for GPUs. The release includes an npm package, demos, and support for PyTorch model conversion and quantization, aiming to streamline deployment of AI models on mobile and desktop web platforms.

entry.title: Essay argues current AI tools focus on task completion without understanding user behavior or productivity patterns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The article discusses how existing AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude excel at completing tasks but lack awareness of users' work habits and productivity rhythms. The author tracked personal activity data over two weeks, revealing patterns such as consistent focus crashes and peak productivity times that AI systems do not detect or address. The piece highlights a gap between AI's task-oriented capabilities and the potential for AI to act as a coach by observing and providing insights into how users work, rather than just what they ask it to do.

entry.title: Deutsche Telekom integrates AI across customer service, employee workflows, and network operations to become an AI-native telecommunications company [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: Deutsche Telekom is transforming its telecommunications operations by embedding AI into customer service, employee workflows, and network management, aiming to become one of the first AI-native telcos. The company serves over 300 million customers and has seen a 546% increase in AI tool usage since early 2026, with more than 50,000 monthly active users of ChatGPT and related APIs. The transformation involves redesigning workflows rather than simply adding AI tools, with initiatives including AI-powered customer care, real-time network optimization, and innovations in voice communications such as live translation and intelligent call assistance. Deutsche Telekom collaborates with OpenAI and other partners to integrate AI directly into everyday communication channels, enhancing customer interactions without requiring new applications. This approach reflects a broader strategy to democratize AI access and embed intelligence into existing telecommunications infrastructure, focusing on operational redesign and balancing leadership direction with employee experimentation to drive adoption and process change.

entry.title: The Information reports on 'eggmaxing,' a fertility trend where women aim to freeze unusually high numbers of eggs, supported by a Silicon Valley group called 'To Make an Omelette'
entry.summary: A private Silicon Valley group chat called "To Make an Omelette" has gathered over 80 women, including tech founders and professionals, who are focused on maximizing their egg freezing efforts, a practice dubbed "eggmaxing." These women, mostly in their 20s and 30s, are pursuing fertility preservation by attempting to freeze dozens or even over 100 eggs, far exceeding typical medical advice of one to two rounds to harvest around 15 eggs for a good chance at having one child. This niche community reflects a growing interest in fertility treatments like in vitro fertilization, which now accounts for more than 2% of U.S. births annually.

entry.title: Researchers explain how AI chatbots can enter delusional spirals causing increasingly inaccurate responses [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: AI chatbots can sometimes produce progressively inaccurate or nonsensical answers in a phenomenon known as a delusional spiral. This occurs because the models generate text based on learned patterns, which can compound errors during extended conversations. Understanding this behavior is important for improving chatbot reliability and user interactions.

entry.title: GenUI launches AI-driven native SwiftUI interface generation with experimental workspace and offline Playground [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: GenUI is an experimental native Swift workspace that uses AI agents to generate declarative SwiftUI interfaces without executing agent-generated code. It includes native iOS and macOS clients, a component catalog, and a local Playground for offline development. The project is structured with multiple Swift packages, protocols, and backend components, supporting cloud and local runtimes. While core builds and offline demos function, hosted gateway features like authentication and rate limiting are still under development. GenUI aims to streamline SwiftUI interface creation by automating design and rendering tasks through AI-generated messages validated against a predefined catalog.

entry.title: Instagram's Adam Mosseri says AI content won't be filtered out but users can avoid it in their feeds if they dislike it [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Instagram head Adam Mosseri stated that the platform will not filter out AI-generated content but will label it to inform users. He suggested that users who do not want AI content can choose not to have it appear in their feeds, while those interested can have feeds focused on AI content. Mosseri acknowledged the difficulty in detecting AI content as models improve and mentioned the possibility of labeling non-AI camera-captured content instead. He also noted Instagram's need to address spammy AI content while continuing to embrace AI features like Meta's Muse Spark image generator.

entry.title: Sunrun launches pilot program to host distributed AI compute nodes in customers' homes, compensating participants and targeting enterprise AI buyers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Sunrun, a solar and home energy storage company, is expanding into AI data centers by launching a pilot program that places small AI compute units in customers' homes equipped with its solar and battery systems. The company plans to compensate participants and sell the distributed compute power to enterprise AI buyers, offering an alternative to traditional centralized data centers amid growing public opposition to new data center construction. The program aims to create a nationwide network of distributed compute nodes, spreading AI infrastructure across many locations rather than concentrating it in large facilities. Sunrun has over 1.1 million customers who can join the pilot waitlist, and the company expects to complete the pilot in the coming months before deciding on a broader rollout. This initiative follows a previous proof of concept and represents a new direction for Sunrun beyond its core energy storage business.

entry.title: Show HN: Tool reverse-engineers web app APIs into reusable AI agent tools without source code access [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A new AI tool automatically converts authenticated web app APIs into reusable "recipes" that enable AI agents to perform actions within applications like Jira, Spotify, and Hacker News without needing source code access. The tool handles authentication, input/output schemas, and adapts to API changes, allowing users to command AI agents to interact directly with apps securely and efficiently. The approach addresses challenges with inconsistent API standards and security methods across modern software, avoiding brittle and slow browser automation. Demonstrations show the AI agent performing tasks faster than traditional point-and-click methods, with app owners enabling discovered tools via a dashboard. The project highlights difficulties with standardizing APIs, especially GraphQL, but aims to simplify AI integration with existing applications.

entry.title: aeovim launches Rust-based AI-powered Neovim-like TUI for managing multiple Claude Code coding agents locally on macOS [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: aeovim is a standalone Rust terminal user interface that applies Neovim's modal editing model to orchestrate multiple live coding agents powered by Claude Code. It allows users to spawn, steer, and review several AI coding sessions simultaneously using familiar Neovim concepts like buffers, tabs, and splits, with session persistence and inter-agent communication features. Currently, aeovim supports multi-turn Claude Code sessions with streaming transcripts, pane navigation, and space management, while planned features include parallel prompt fan-out to multiple agents, a task board, Vim-style diff review, and syntax highlighting. The project is installable via Cargo and designed for single-user local use on macOS, with a focus on keyboard-native workflows and extensibility for other AI backends in the future.

How to Conduct a Competitive Analysis with Google Gemini [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Decisions about when, where, and how to expand a business are always fraught with uncertainty. The prospect of growing the business and reaching new customers with novel offerings is enticing, but a false step can be extremely costly. A well-researched competitive analysis can reduce this risk by surfacing potential stumbling blocks at the very beginning of the brainstorming process. Historically, these analyses have been extremely time-consuming, as they have required business leaders to manually look through hundreds of pages of annual reports, painstakingly track competitor pricing, and synthesize consumer sentiment from social media and review websites. With Gemini, organizations can quickly generate an initial competitive analysis report, helping leaders decide whether a new venture is worth pursuing. Step 1: Prompt Gemini To get the best results, you'll want to be as specific as possible. Consider using a prompt that gives Gemini a persona and a clear objective, which will help ensure that Gemini approaches the task from the viewpoint of a business leader, rather than a casual searcher. Here's an example: I am a CMO conducting a competitive analysis. My company is considering expanding into [a new line of business]. Generate a list of the top five competitors in the [industry] industry and include their pricing, strengths, weaknesses, and target audience. If you type your prompt into the "Ask Gemini" box, Gemini will return a high-level briefing in just a few seconds. If you want something more comprehensive, click on the "Tools" button and select "Deep Research," then run your prompt. Gemini will create a research plan. Review the plan, suggest any needed tweaks, and then click "Start Research." For a Deep Research report, Gemini will produce a competitive analysis with citations and sources. Step 2: Interrogate the Output Gemini's initial response or report should be treated as a starting point, not a finished analysis. While the model can quickly surface competitors, pricing models, and positioning, you still need to use your own industry and market expertise to evaluate and refine those insights. First, simply check to make sure that Gemini's output aligns with your knowledge of the space. Is the list of competitors complete, or are any key players missing? Does the pricing reflect what you've seen in the real world? Ask Gemini to fill in any gaps. You might go back and forth several times, with each response containing more complete and nuanced information. This iterative process helps ensure that Gemini delivers the exact details you need to determine how to move forward. Step 3: Create a Five-Year Plan Once you have a clearer picture of the competitive landscape, you can begin to map out a strategic direction. Here again, Gemini can get you started. Try this sample prompt: Okay, I am going to try to convince my CEO that we should expand into [line of business]. Draft a concise, competitive strategy outline for the next five years for the [industry] industry across North American markets with potential goals, strategies, and tactics. You can also add any relevant sources so Gemini has more information about your organization. Gemini's plan may include initial goals for market penetration, specific tactics to support strategic pillars, and a year-by-year execution roadmap. Just as with the competitive analysis report, you should bring your own judgment and expertise to this five-year plan. Build on what you find helpful, and push back on areas that feel weak or impractical. Keep working with Gemini until you have an outline that is both realistic and aligned with your goals. Step 4: Make the Work Your Own Before presenting your expansion plan to leadership, revise it to include essential details that aren't included in Gemini's training data: your internal capabilities, budget constraints, existing customer relationships, and leadership priorities. Replace any generic language with details grounded in your market knowledge, and adjust timelines or tactics based on what your team can realistically execute. You may also want to incorporate case studies or data points from your company's previous efforts to strengthen your case. With Gemini, you can complete the comprehensive background work needed for an expansion effort that succeeds in the real world.

entry.title: The new GPT-5.6 family: Luna, Terra, Sol [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI's latest flagship model hit general availability this morning, and comes in three sizes: Luna, Terra, and Sol (from smallest to largest). The new models are priced per 1M input/output tokens as Luna $1/$6, Terra $2.50/$15, Sol $5/$30. For comparison, the Claude Opus series are $5/$25 and the Claude Fable 5 is $10/$50, but price-per-million tokens doesn't tell us much now that the number of reasoning tokens can differ so much between models for the same task. All three models have a February 16th 2026 knowledge cutoff, a million token context window, and 128,000 maximum output tokens. OpenAI's biggest benchmark claim concerns long-running agentic performance, with one benchmark showing all three models outperforming Claude Fable 5: We trained GPT-5.6 to get more useful work from every token. On Agents' Last Exam, an evaluation of long-running professional workflows across 55 fields, GPT-5.6 Sol sets a new high of 53.6, eclipsing Claude Fable 5 (adaptive reasoning) by 13.1 points. Even at medium reasoning, it beats Fable 5 by 11.4 points at roughly one-quarter the estimated cost. That efficiency extends to smaller models, which are essential to making intelligence more abundant and affordable: GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-5.6 Luna outperform Fable 5 at around one-sixteenth the cost. Amusingly, one self-reported benchmark that Fable 5 crushed the GPT-5.6 family on was SWE-Bench Pro, where Fable 5 got 80% compared to GPT-5.6 Sol getting 64.6%. This may help explain why OpenAI chose to publish this article yesterday specifically calling out SWE-Bench Pro for problems they found while auditing that benchmark: In light of these results, we estimate that ~30% of SWE-bench Pro tasks are broken, and advise that model developers carefully examine results I've had some early access to GPT-5.6 Sol - it's definitely very competent, though so far it hasn't struck me as better than Fable at the kind of complex coding tasks I've been using with Anthropic's model. As usual, the model guidance for using GPT-5.6 has the most interesting details. There are a bunch of new API features that I need to explore (and probably add support for in LLM), including: Programmatic Tool Calling allows the models to "compose and run JavaScript that orchestrates tool calls" - which sounds to me like it could help bridge the gap between MCPs and full terminal sessions that can compose CLI utilities in useful ways. Also reminiscent of the dynamic filtering mechanism Anthropic added to their web search tool, which allows code execution against web results as part of a single model turn. Multi-agent lets the model "spin up subagents for parallel, focused work" - the sub-agent pattern now baked into the core API. Prompt cache breakpoints brings the Claude model of prompt caching to OpenAI, letting you be explicit about where the cache breakpoints are rather than relying on the API to detect them automatically. Personally I much prefer automatic detection (still supported by OpenAI), but presumably there are optimization cost savings to be had here if you put the work in. You can now set detail: original on image requests to avoid resizing the image at all before it is processed. Here's a full page with 18 different pelicans - for reasoning efforts none, low, medium, high, xhigh, and max across the three different models. It also lists their token and calculated costs - the least expensive was gpt-5.6-luna at effort none for 0.71 cents, the most expensive was gpt-5.6-sol at max reasoning level for 48.55 cents. In further pelican news, if you jump to 17:50 in their livestream from this morning you'll see OpenAI's own demo of 3D pelicans riding a tricycle, a bicycle, a pony, and another pelican!
